questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A metal fabricator and manufacturer entered into a contract for the sale of a plasma cutter made by the manufacturer. While the manufacturer had several plasma cutters on hand, the contract provided for the sale of a particular plasma cutter identified by its serial number. The contract specified that the manufacturer would ship the cutter by a third-party carrier. However, the contract did not specify who was to pay the costs of transportation nor the place of tender for the plasma cutter. The manufacturer shipped the cutter identified in the contract to the fabricator via a carrier under a proper contract for its transportation. The carrier delivered the cutter to the fabricator, and the fabricator verified that the cutter delivered was the one specified in the contract.
Under these facts, when did the risk of loss pass to the fabricator?

choices.A: When the contract was made.
choices.B: When the cutter was delivered to the carrier and a proper contract for its transportation was made.
choices.C: When the cutter was unloaded on the fabricator's premises by the carrier.
choices.D: When the fabricator verified that the cutter delivered was the cutter specified in the contract.

questions.explanation:
Risk of loss in the absence of breach
(UCC § 2-509)
General rule
  • If seller is merchant, risk of loss passes to buyer when buyer takes physical possession of goods
  • If not, risk of loss passes to buyer when seller satisfies contractual delivery obligations
Goods to be shipped by carrier
  • Shipment contract (presumed) – risk of loss passes to buyer when goods are given to carrier & proper contract for shipment is made
  • Destination contract – risk of loss passes to buyer when goods are delivered at place specified in contract
Goods to be held by bailee
  • Risk of loss passes to buyer when:
    • buyer receives negotiable document of title covering goods (e.g., warehouse receipt) or
    • bailee (e.g., warehouseman) acknowledges buyer's right to possess goods
UCC = Uniform Commercial Code.

Contracts for the sale of goods (e.g., plasma cutter) are governed by the Uniform Commercial Code (UCC). Under the UCC, the risk of loss in the absence of a breach generally passes to the buyer when the buyer receives the goods. But if the contract requires the seller to deliver the goods through a third-party carrier, then the risk of loss passes to the buyer at different times depending on whether the contract is a:

  • shipment contract – a contract that does not require delivery at a particular location, in which case the risk of loss passes to the buyer when the goods are delivered to the carrier and a proper contract for their shipment is made or
  • destination contract – a contract that requires delivery at a particular location, in which case the risk of loss passes to the buyer when the goods are delivered at the named location.

Here, the contract required shipment by a third-party carrier. Because the contract did not specify a delivery location, it is presumed to be a shipment contract. Accordingly, the risk of loss shifted to the fabricator when the plasma cutter was delivered to the carrier and a proper contract for its transportation was made (Choices A and C).

(Choice D) The risk of loss remains with the seller when a tender or delivery of goods is so nonconforming that the buyer has the right to reject them. But here, the manufacturer shipped conforming goods. The fabricator did not need to first verify that the cutter delivered was the cutter specified in the contract before the risk of loss could pass to the fabricator.

📌 Educational Objective

In a shipment contract, the risk of loss shifts to the buyer when the seller delivers the goods to a third-party carrier and makes a proper contract for their shipment.

📚 References
  • UCC § 2-509 (providing rules for risk of loss in absence of breach).
questions.zh-question: 一家金属加工商和一家制造商签订了一份合同，约定销售由该制造商生产的一台等离子切割机。尽管制造商手头有几台等离子切割机，但合同规定销售一台通过序列号识别的特定等离子切割机。合同规定制造商将通过第三方承运人发货。然而，合同没有明确运输费用由谁支付，也没有明确等离子切割机的交货地点（place of tender）。制造商通过承运人，根据一份适当的运输合同，将合同中指定的切割机运送给了加工商。承运人将切割机交付给加工商，加工商核实所交付的切割机正是合同中指定的那一台。在这些事实下，损失风险（risk of loss）何时转移给加工商？

zh-choices.A: 合同签订时。
zh-choices.B: 切割机交付给承运人并签订了适当的运输合同时。
zh-choices.C: 承运人将切割机卸载到加工商的场所时。
zh-choices.D: 加工商核实所交付的切割机是合同中指定的切割机时。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Performance, Breach, and Discharge - Other performance matters

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：货物买卖中的风险转移（risk of loss），看的是卖方把货交给第三方承运人时，风险什么时候从卖方转到买方。

三秒认题路径：

卖货合同 → 承运人运输 → 无交货地 → 推定装运合同 → 交承运人即转风险

核心法律规则

UCC § 2-509 处理的是没有违约时的风险转移。一般来说，卖方是商人时，买方拿到货物占有时才转风险；但只要合同要求通过第三方承运人运输，考试先判断是装运合同（shipment contract）还是目的地合同（destination contract）。装运合同（shipment contract）的考场意思：卖方把货交给承运人并做出正确运输安排，风险就先转给买方。

目的地合同（destination contract）的考场意思：必须等货到合同指定地点，风险才转。这里合同没有写具体交货地点，所以默认是装运合同；卖方把这台按序列号识别的 plasma cutter 交给承运人并办妥运输后，风险已经转给买方，不用等买方到场验货。

核心判例： 题干直接套用 UCC § 2-509 的默认规则：未指定交货地点时，推定为装运合同，货交承运人且运输合同适当成立时，风险即转移。

思维导图

1. 先看是不是终局后才讨论：不是，这是 货物风险转移 题。
关卡 1：合同是否要求承运人运输？
YES：继续分装运合同 / 目的地合同
关卡 2：题干有没有写“送到某个指定地点”？
NO：推定为 shipment contract
关卡 3：卖方是否已把这件货交给承运人，并签好正确运输合同？
YES：风险当场转给买方 → 选 B
被排除的想法：买方验收 不是这里的触发点；本题不是看谁先确认货物无误，而是看运输合同类型和交付时点。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：货已经到买方门口，应该等买方验收后才转风险。

但考试真正问的是：合同是不是 shipment contract，以及卖方是否已把货交给承运人并办妥运输。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干写明未约定交货地点，却指定由第三方承运人运输，默认是 shipment contract；所以货交承运人且运输合同成立时，风险已转给买方。

❌ 概念混淆 | 验收时点误判

✕ A: 把一般交货规则硬套进承运运输，忽略了装运合同的特殊时点。

❌ 法律适用 | 到货地点误套

✕ C: 看到 unloaded 就以为到门口才转风险，但题干没写目的地合同。

❌ 事实误判 | 验货条件偷加

✕ D: 硬加买方先验货的条件，题干只说确认货对版，不是风险转移门槛。

这题建议用什么方法？

先定运输合同类型，再看交付给承运人的瞬间，别被“买方验货”带偏。

考场速记

记住一句：有承运人、无指定交货地，先按 shipment contract 想；货一交承运人，风险就多半已经转给买方了。

如果题目真要考中间上诉，再想口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely，对应 injunction、certification、class action 等法定例外。

question_analysis.micro_concept: UCC shipment contract risk of loss
question_analysis.skill_tested: Determine risk of loss transfer under UCC carrier contracts

label.zh: 统一商法典第二编适用性

reason.en: Establishes that the transaction involves a sale of goods, triggering UCC rules rather than common law.
reason.zh: 确立该交易涉及货物买卖，从而触发统一商法典（UCC）而非普通法规则。

keywords.text: ship the cutter by a third-party carrier

reason.en: Triggers the specific UCC risk of loss rules for goods shipped by a third-party carrier.
reason.zh: 触发UCC中关于通过第三方承运人运输货物的特定损失风险转移规则。

keywords.text: did not specify who was to pay the costs of transportation nor the place of tender

reason.en: Under the UCC, when a carrier is used but no delivery location is specified, the contract is presumed to be a shipment contract.
reason.zh: 根据UCC，当使用承运人但未指定送达地点时，该合同被推定为装运合同（Shipment Contract）。

reason.en: Fulfills the seller's duty under a shipment contract to make a reasonable contract for transport.
reason.zh: 履行了卖方在装运合同下订立合理运输合同的义务。

reason.en: Incorrectly suggests risk of loss passes upon contract formation, which is not the rule for goods requiring shipment.
reason.zh: 错误地认为损失风险在合同成立时转移，这不适用于需要运输的货物。

B.text: delivered to the carrier and a proper contract for its transportation was made

reason.en: Correctly identifies the moment risk of loss passes to the buyer in a shipment contract.
reason.zh: 正确指出了在装运合同中损失风险转移给买方的时刻。

reason.en: Applies the rule for destination contracts, which does not apply here because no specific delivery location was agreed upon.
reason.zh: 适用了目的地合同的规则，但由于双方未约定具体送达地点，该规则在此不适用。

D.text: verified that the cutter delivered was the cutter specified

reason.en: Confuses the buyer's right to inspect conforming goods with the timing of the risk of loss transfer.
reason.zh: 混淆了买方检验符合合同货物的权利与损失风险转移的时点。

highlights.text: the contract specified that the manufacturer would ship the cutter by a third-party carrier.

reason.en: Establishes that the contract involves shipment by a carrier, narrowing the risk of loss rules to UCC § 2-509(1).
reason.zh: 确立了合同涉及通过承运人运输，从而将损失风险规则缩小至UCC § 2-509(1)。

highlights.text: the contract did not specify who was to pay the costs of transportation nor the place of tender

reason.en: Triggers the UCC presumption that the agreement is a shipment contract rather than a destination contract.
reason.zh: 触发UCC推定，即该协议为装运合同而非目的地合同。

highlights.text: when did the risk of loss pass to the fabricator?

label.zh: 损失风险转移时点问题

reason.en: The core legal question to be resolved based on the shipment contract rules.
reason.zh: 需要根据装运合同规则解决的核心法律问题。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A seller entered into a contract with a buyer to sell a house for a price of $150,000. The contract contained the following clause: "This contract is conditional on the buyer securing bank financing at an interest rate of 7% or below." The buyer did not make an application for bank financing and therefore did not secure it and refused to proceed with the purchase. The seller sued the buyer for breach of contract.
Is the seller likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because the buyer did not secure bank financing.
choices.B: No, because the contract did not expressly impose on the buyer any obligation to apply for bank financing.
choices.C: Yes, because a court will excuse the condition to avoid a disproportionate forfeiture.
choices.D: Yes, because a court will imply a term imposing on the buyer a duty to use reasonable efforts to secure bank financing.

questions.explanation:
Contract conditions
Condition precedent停止条件 / 先决条件 (在特定未来的不确定事件发生之前，当事人的履行义务不产生) Uncertain future event that, if it occurs, creates party's obligation to perform (e.g., A agrees to hire B if B graduates college)
Condition subsequent解除条件 / 后续条件 (特定未来的不确定事件一旦发生，便解除当事人已存在的履行义务) Uncertain future event that, if it occurs, excuses party's existing obligation to perform (e.g., B agrees to work for C until B graduates college)

Performance is generally due once a contract is formed. However, performance can be delayed or discharged by a condition—ie, an uncertain future event that must occur before performance becomes due or is discharged. There are two types of conditions:

  • condition precedent* – delays performance until a specified event occurs
  • condition subsequent – excuses performance once a specified event occurs

A condition precedent will be excused if a party whose performance is subject to that condition wrongfully prevents the condition from occurring—eg, by breaching the implied duty of good faith and fair dealing. As a result, the condition no longer must occur for that party's performance to become due.

Here, the buyer's performance was delayed by the condition that he secured financing at an interest rate of 7% or below. The implied duty of good faith and fair dealing required the buyer to make reasonable efforts to secure financing. He breached that duty by making no effort to secure financing, so the condition precedent was excused and the buyer's performance became due. Therefore, the seller is likely to prevail (Choices A & B).

*A condition concurrent arises when each party's obligation to perform is a condition precedent to the other party's obligation to perform (ie, when performance is due simultaneously).

(Choice C) The seller would not be subject to any significant forfeiture (ie, loss of benefit or right) if the buyer's condition to obtain financing is not excused. That is because the seller can sell the house to someone else.

📌 Educational Objective

A condition precedent will be excused if a party whose performance is subject to that condition wrongfully prevents the condition from occurring—eg, by breaching the implied duty of good faith and fair dealing.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts §§ 224–25 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (conditions and effect of nonoccurrence).
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 229 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (excuse of condition to avoid forfeiture).
questions.zh-question:
卖方与买方签订合同，以150,000美元的价格出售一栋房屋。合同包含以下条款：“本合同以买方获得利率为7%或以下的银行融资为条件。”买方未申请银行融资，因此未能获得融资，并拒绝继续进行购买。卖方向法院起诉买方违约。

卖方是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为买方未能获得银行融资。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为合同没有明确规定买方有申请银行融资的义务。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为法院将免除该条件以避免不成比例的权利丧失。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为法院将默示一个条款，规定买方有义务尽合理努力去获得银行融资。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Performance, Breach, and Discharge - Timing of Conditions

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：买卖合同里把 融资成功（condition precedent） 写成先决条件后，买方故意什么都不做，法院会不会把这个条件“掰掉”，让买方履行义务照样到期。

三秒认题路径：

先决条件 → 买方不申请 → 失信阻止 → 条件被免除 → 卖方可赢

核心法律规则

先决条件（condition precedent）的意思是：某个不确定未来事件不发生，履行义务就先不来。后续条件（condition subsequent）则相反，是事件一发生，原本存在的义务被解除。

如果一方对该条件的发生负有配合义务，却故意不配合，法院会认定该条件被 免除（excused），因为不能让自己先阻止条件成就，再拿条件没成就当挡箭牌。

本题里，买方明知要靠贷款成就履约，却连申请都不交，这就是违反 善意与公平交易义务（good faith and fair dealing），所以融资这个先决条件被免除，买方付款义务到期，卖方能赢。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts §§ 224-25, 229 — 先决条件可因一方错误阻止其成就而被免除，避免其借自己制造的失败逃避履约。

思维导图

合同先写了什么？
“买方拿到 7%及以下融资 才算成交”
第一步：这是 先决条件（condition precedent），不是随便的背景事实。
买方有没有配合条件成就？
题干事实：买方 没有申请贷款。
卡死点：自己不努力 = 错误阻止条件成就
结果会怎样？
法律后果：条件被免除 → 买方履行义务到期 → 卖方可主张违约。
答案：D

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然 did not secure 融资，那买方就不用买了。

但考试真正问的是：这个“没贷到款”是不是买方自己故意造成的；如果是，条件不能拿来救他。

这里不是在问“结果有没有发生”，而是在问“买方能不能靠自己造成的失败逃掉履行”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干 连贷款申请都没做，说明买方主动阻止了先决条件成就；法院会补上 合理努力（reasonable efforts） 义务，所以卖方可胜。

❌ 事实误判 | 只看未成就

✕ A: 只盯着 did not secure，忽略了这是买方自己没做事。

❌ 法律适用 | 忽略默示义务

✕ B: 以为没写 apply 就没义务，其实善意义务会补进去。

❌ 概念混淆 | 误套免除

✕ C: 把 forfeiture 当成万能逃生门，但卖方还能转卖，没到要免除条件的程度。

这题建议用什么方法？

先找条件类型，再看谁在阻止条件成就；只要是自己把门关上，就别想拿门关着当理由。

考场速记

记住一句：先决条件（condition precedent）可以因为一方故意阻止而被免除；看到“我没申请、所以我不用履行”，先想 good faith and fair dealing。

这题的速记法就是：“先决条件被自己卡死，就不能拿卡死当借口。”

question_analysis.skill_tested: Analyze excuse of condition precedent

reason.en: Indicates that performance obligations depend on a future uncertain event.
reason.zh: 表明履行义务取决于未来的不确定事件。

reason.en: Shows the buyer failed to act to satisfy the condition, triggering excuse by prevention.
reason.zh: 表明买方未采取行动促成条件达成，从而触发因阻碍而免除条件的规则。

reason.en: The legal claim brought by the seller against the buyer.
reason.zh: 卖方起诉买方的法律诉求。

reason.en: Distractor focusing on the literal non-occurrence of the condition while ignoring the buyer's lack of effort.
reason.zh: 干扰项，仅关注条件字面上未成就，而忽略了买方未做出努力的事实。

reason.en: Distractor arguing that a duty must be express, ignoring implied covenants of good faith.
reason.zh: 干扰项，主张义务必须明示，忽略了默示的诚信交易协定。

reason.en: An incorrect doctrine for excusing conditions, as selling to another is not a forfeiture.
reason.zh: 错误的免除条件规则，因为卖给他人并不构成没收或重大损失。

reason.en: Reflects the court's implication of a duty to use reasonable efforts under good faith.
reason.zh: 反映了法院根据诚信原则默示买方负有合理努力的义务。

highlights.text: conditional on the buyer securing bank financing

reason.en: Establishes the condition that must be met before performance is due.
reason.zh: 确立了履行前必须满足的先决条件。

highlights.text: did not make an application for bank financing

reason.en: Shows the buyer made zero effort, which prevents the condition's occurrence.
reason.zh: 表明买方完全未做出努力，从而阻碍了条件的成就。

highlights.text: Is the seller likely to prevail

reason.en: Asks whether the buyer's failure to apply excuses the condition and makes them liable.
reason.zh: 询问买方未申请贷款是否免除了条件的成就并使其承担责任。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A lumber supplier agreed to sell to a furniture manufacturer all the lumber that the manufacturer required over a two-year period. The sales contract provided that payment was due 60 days after delivery, but that a 3% discount would be allowed if the manufacturer paid within 10 days of delivery. During the first year of the contract, the manufacturer regularly paid within the 10-day period and received the 3% discount.
Fifteen days after the supplier had made its most recent lumber delivery to the manufacturer, the supplier had received no payment from the manufacturer. At this time, the supplier became aware of rumors from a credible source that the manufacturer's financial condition was precarious. The supplier wrote the manufacturer, demanding assurances regarding the manufacturer's financial status. The manufacturer immediately mailed to the supplier its latest audited financial statements as well as a satisfactory credit report prepared by the manufacturer's banker. The rumors proved to be false. Nevertheless, the supplier refused to resume deliveries. The manufacturer has sued the supplier for breach of contract.
Will the manufacturer likely prevail?

choices.A: No, because the contract was unenforceable, since the manufacturer had not committed to purchase a definite quantity of lumber.
choices.B: No, because the supplier had reasonable grounds for insecurity and was therefore entitled to cancel the contract and refuse to make any future deliveries.
choices.C: Yes, because the credit report and audited financial statements provided adequate assurance of due performance under the contract.
choices.D: Yes, because the supplier was not entitled to condition resumption of deliveries on the receipt of financial status information.

questions.explanation:
Under the UCC, a party with reasonable grounds for insecurity about the other party's performance has the right to make a written demand for assurances that the other party will perform. The insecure party may also suspend its own performance until assurance is provided. Between merchants, the reasonableness of insecurity and the adequacy of assurance are determined by commercial standards (eg, financial status information). Failure to provide adequate assurance within 30 days after a valid demand constitutes an anticipatory repudiation.

Here, the supplier had reasonable grounds for insecurity about the manufacturer's ability to pay after being told by a credible source that the manufacturer's financial condition was precarious. As a result, the supplier was entitled to condition resumption of deliveries on the receipt of adequate assurance (Choice D). The manufacturer provided adequate assurance with its audited financial statements and credit report. Therefore, the supplier was not entitled to cancel the contract, and the manufacturer will likely prevail in its breach-of-contract suit (Choice B).

(Choice A) Contracts for the sale of goods (eg, lumber) must contain a quantity term数量条款 (A contract term stating the amount of goods to be sold). Here, the contract did not specify a definite quantity of lumber. But the quantity could be made certain under this requirements contract需求合同 (A contract in which a seller agrees to provide all of a buyer's needs) because the supplier agreed to deliver all the lumber the manufacturer required over a two-year period.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the UCC, a party with reasonable grounds for insecurity about the other party's performance has the right to make a written demand for assurances that the other party will perform. Between merchants, the reasonableness of insecurity and the adequacy of assurance are determined by commercial standards.

UCC = Uniform Commercial Code

📚 References
  • U.C.C. § 2-609 (Am. Law Inst. & Unif. Law Comm'n 2020) (right to adequate assurance of performance).
questions.zh-question:
一家木材供应商同意在两年期内，向一家家具制造商出售其所需的所有木材。销售合同规定，货款应在交货后60天内付清，但如果制造商在交货后10天内付款，则可享受3%的折扣。在合同的第一年，制造商定期在10天内付款，并获得了3%的折扣。

在供应商最近一次向制造商交付木材15天后，供应商仍未收到制造商的任何付款。此时，供应商从一个可靠来源获悉，该制造商的财务状况岌岌可可危。供应商致函制造商，要求其就财务状况提供保证。制造商立即向供应商邮寄了其最新的经审计的财务报表，以及由制造商的银行出具的令人满意的信用报告。这些谣言后来被证明是假的。然而，供应商拒绝恢复交货。制造商已起诉供应商违约。

制造商是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为合同不可执行，原因是制造商没有承诺购买确定数量的木材。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为供应商有合理理由感到不安，因此有权解除合同并拒绝未来任何交货。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为信用报告和经审计的财务报表为合同的适当履行提供了充分的保证。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为供应商无权将恢复交货的条件建立在收到财务状况信息之上。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Performance, Breach, and Discharge - Anticipatory Repudiation

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：UCC 适格商人在对方财务状况让自己起疑时，能不能发出书面担保要求（written demand for assurances），以及对方已经给出足够担保后，自己还能不能继续拒绝履行。

三秒认题路径：

卖货合同 → 财务起疑 → 要求担保 → 已给材料 → 不能拒履

核心法律规则

《统一商法典》（UCC）下，只要一方对对方履约有合理不安（reasonable grounds for insecurity），就可以发出书面担保要求（written demand for adequate assurances）。考场意思：你先别急着毁约，先看对方有没有把“我会照做”说清楚、说够。商人（merchants）之间，是否不安、担保够不够，都按商业标准看。

如果对方在法定期限内给出足够担保，就不能把这件事当成预期违约（anticipatory repudiation）。考场意思：对方已经把风险压下去了，你这边就不能借题发挥停摆到底。

核心判例： U.C.C. § 2-609 — 这条规则直接锁定：担保要求成立，但对方及时提供了足够担保，所以拒绝继续履行的一方会输。

思维导图

先看：卖方有没有合理理由担心买方会不会付款？
有可发出书面担保要求（written demand for assurances），并可先暂停自己继续交货。
再看买方有没有在合理期限内给出足够担保？
本题卡点：买方交了审计财报 + 银行信用报告，足够担保已到位。
结论卖方不能再拒绝履行，继续停供会构成违约，买方胜。
别被带偏“已经听到坏消息”只说明能提要求，不代表能直接取消合同。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然卖方已经听到可信来源说买方财务危险，那它当然能直接拒绝后续交货。

但考试真正问的是：买方后来有没有给出足够担保；一旦担保到位，卖方就不能把“担心”直接升级成“拒供”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干里卖方发出担保要求后，买方立刻交了审计财报 + 银行信用报告，这就是足够担保，所以卖方不能继续拒绝交货。

❌ 概念混淆 | 数量条款误判

✕ A: 把quantity term问题硬塞进来，但本题已是需求合同。

❌ 法律适用 | 直接取消误判

✕ B: 以为起疑就能立刻停供到底，忽略了对方已补足担保。

❌ 事实误判 | 担保内容误读

✕ D: 把financial status information当成不够，其实它正好用来消除疑虑。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“合理不安”，再看“是否已给足够担保”，不要把起疑直接等同于可拒绝履行。

考场速记

记住一句：起疑可以要担保，担保到位就得继续履行。看到 UCC 的担保要求题，先问“有没有合理不安”，再问“对方有没有及时补救”。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A tech company contracted with a private university to sell and deliver to the university a mainframe computer using a new type of technology then under development but not perfected by the company, at a price substantially lower than that of a similar computer using current technology. After making the contract with the university, the tech company discovered that the new technology it intended to use was unreliable and that no computer manufacturer could yet build a reliable computer using that technology.
The tech company thereupon notified the university that it was impossible for the tech company or anyone else to build the contracted-for computer "in the present state of the art."
If the university sues the tech company for failure to perform its computer contract, which party will the court most likely find in favor of?

choices.A: The tech company, because a contract to build a machine using technology under development imposes only a duty on the builder to use its best efforts to achieve the result contracted for.
choices.B: The tech company, because its performance of the contract was objectively impossible.
choices.C: The university, because the law of impossibility does not apply to merchants under the applicable law.
choices.D: The university, because the tech company assumed the risk, in the given circumstances, that the projected new technology would not work reliably.

questions.explanation:
Commercial impracticability
(UCC § 2-615)

Seller's delay in delivery or nondelivery (in whole or in part) excused if:

  • unanticipated or extraordinary event made it impossible or commercially impracticable for seller to perform as agreed
  • nonoccurrence of event was basic assumption of contract
  • seller did not assume risk of event's occurrence (eg, by contractual language)
UCC = Uniform Commercial Code

Contracts for the sale of goods (eg, computers) are governed by Article 2 of the Uniform Commercial Code (UCC). Under the UCC, the doctrine of impracticability will excuse a seller's* nonperformance (eg, late or nondelivery of goods) if:

  • an unanticipated or extraordinary event made it impossible or commercially impracticable for the seller to perform as agreed (Choice C) and
  • the contract was formed under a basic assumption that the event would not occur.

But this doctrine does not apply if the seller assumed the risk of the event—eg, the circumstances indicate that the seller foresaw the risk yet failed to make contractual provision for it.

Here, after entering the contract with the university, the tech company learned that the new technology it intended to use was unreliable and that it was impossible to build the contracted-for computer. However, there is always a foreseeable risk that new technology will not work reliably. Since the tech company failed to make contractual provision for this risk, it assumed the risk that the new technology would fail. Therefore, the tech company's failure to perform will not be excused for impracticability, and the court will likely find for the university (Choice B).

*Under the UCC, impracticability almost always affects the seller (not the buyer) because the buyer's only obligation is to pay for the goods.

(Choice A) There is no rule that a contract to build a machine using technology under development imposes only a duty on the builder to use its "best efforts" to achieve the contracted-for result.

📌 Educational Objective

The UCC's doctrine of impracticability does not apply, and a party's performance will not be excused, if the party assumed the risk of the event giving rise to the impracticability.

📚 References
  • U.C.C. § 2-615 (Am. Law Inst. & Unif. Law Comm'n 2020) (excuse by failure of presupposed conditions).
questions.zh-question:
一家科技公司与一所私立大学签订合同，向该大学出售并交付一台使用该公司当时正在开发但尚未完善的新型技术的大型计算机，价格远低于使用现有技术的同类计算机。与大学签订合同后，该科技公司发现其原计划使用的技术并不可靠，且目前没有任何计算机制造商能够使用该技术制造出可靠的计算机。

该科技公司于是通知该大学，称对于该公司或任何其他人来说，在“现有技术水平下”制造合同约定的大型计算机是不可能的。

如果大学因该科技公司未能履行其计算机合同而提起诉讼，法院最有可能支持哪一方？

zh-choices.A: 科技公司，因为一份制造使用开发中技术的机器的合同，仅对制造商施加了尽最大努力去实现合同约定结果的义务。
zh-choices.B: 科技公司，因为其履行合同在客观上是不可能的。
zh-choices.C: 大学，因为根据适用法律，“不可能”原则不适用于商人。
zh-choices.D: 大学，因为在既定情况下，该科技公司承担了预想中的新技术无法可靠运行的风险。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Performance, Breach, and Discharge - Performance, Breach, and Discharge

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：UCC下卖方遇到新技术失败时，能不能用 商业上不切实际（commercial impracticability） 免责，以及“已经预见风险却没写进合同”会不会把免责挡回去。

三秒认题路径：

卖货合同 → 新技术失败 → 想用免责 → 看是否担责 → 选买方赢

核心法律规则

货物买卖合同（contract for sale of goods） 受 UCC Article 2 约束，所以先看 商业上不切实际（commercial impracticability）。规则很简单：只有当意外或异常事件让履行变得不可能或明显不划算，而且该事件不是合同的基本前提、卖方也没有承担这个风险时，卖方才可能免责。

如果卖方明知 新技术（new technology） 还没成熟，却仍按这个前提签约，考试里通常会说它已经 assumed the risk，所以不能把失败推给 impracticability。也就是说，能不能免责，不看“后来多惨”，看的是“签约时是不是自己把这个坑接下来了”。

核心判例： UCC § 2-615 的思路是：免责只给没承担风险的一方；像本题这种明知技术未成熟还照签的卖方，通常不能靠 impracticability 脱身。

思维导图

这是不是 UCC 货物买卖？
是先用 商业上不切实际（commercial impracticability） 看卖方能否免责。
有没有 异常事件 让履行失败？
有再问：这个风险是不是合同的基本前提？
关键卡点：卖方有没有 承担风险（assume the risk）？
本题直接卡死在这里：卖方知道新技术不成熟，却没把风险写进合同，所以不能免责。
结论履行失败不被 excused，法院找 大学（university） 赢。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：技术都已经坏到“谁也做不出来”，那不就是 impossible 吗？

但考试真正问的是：卖方签约时有没有把“新技术可能翻车”这件事自己接下去。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

本题的坑在于把“后来发现做不成”误当成自动免责；其实只要风险本来就可预见，而且卖方没做合同安排，免责就可能被堵住。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干 明知新技术还不成熟却照样签约，说明卖方已经把失败风险接下了，所以不能用 commercial impracticability 免责。

❌ 概念混淆 | best efforts误判

✕ A: 把 best efforts 当成机器开发合同的默认规则了。

❌ 法律适用 | 客观不能误判

✕ B: 只看到 objectively impossible，却漏了风险已由卖方承担。

❌ 事实误判 | merchant限制误读

✕ C: 乱加 merchants 限制，题干根本没这个条件。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是不是 UCC 卖货合同，再查卖方是否已把技术失败风险自己接住。

考场速记

记住一句话：impracticability 不是“做不到就一定免责”，而是“做不到且没自担风险”才可能免责。

本题速记：预见风险却不写进合同 = 自己扛；自己扛了，就别想拿 impracticability 走人。

reason.en: Shows the seller knew the technology was not yet reliable at formation.
reason.zh: 表明卖方在合同成立时明知该技术尚未完善。

reason.en: Price discount confirms the risk was factored into the bargain.
reason.zh: 价格折扣证实了该风险已被计入交易考量。

reason.en: The event that rendered the performance impossible.

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
On October 30, a customer entered a retail beauty supply store to purchase hair dye to color her hair for Halloween. The clerk who helped the customer was hired the previous day and was not trained regarding different types of dye. The customer explained that she wanted a washable dye, as she had a presentation the following day at work and needed to look professional for it. The clerk showed the customer a permanent hair dye, assuring the customer that the dye was appropriate for her needs. The clerk then told the customer that because the dye was on sale, it was being sold "as is," and that she could not be responsible for any adverse reactions. The customer made the purchase and used the dye to color her hair. The customer could not wash out the dye from her hair on the morning of November 1. As a consequence, the customer lost an account because she could not deliver the presentation.
In a breach-of-warranty action against the store, will the customer likely prevail?

choices.A: No, because the clerk was not a merchant.
choices.B: No, because the clerk's statement that the dye was sold "as is" disclaimed any warranties.
choices.C: Yes, because the clerk's promise created an express warranty.
choices.D: Yes, because the warranty of fitness for a particular purpose cannot be disclaimed.

questions.explanation:
Warranties in sale-of-goods contracts
Implied Merchantability Goods are reasonably fit for their ordinary purpose & pass without objection in trade under contract description—if seller is merchant
Fitness for particular purpose Goods are fit for particular purpose—if seller has reason to know buyer is relying on seller's skill or judgment to select goods
Express Any affirmation, promise, description, or sample made by seller regarding goods that is part of basis of bargain

Under the UCC, a seller of goods creates an express warranty by making any promise or affirmation regarding the goods that becomes part of the basis of the bargain. However, a seller does not create an express warranty by merely giving her opinion or praising the value of the goods.

Here, the customer explained that she needed a washable dye, and the clerk assured the customer that the dye was appropriate for her needs. The clerk's assurance, which constituted a promise or affirmation, created an express warranty. The warranty was breached because the dye was permanent, not washable. Therefore, the customer will likely prevail in a breach-of-warranty action against the store.

(Choice A) Any seller, including a nonmerchant, may create an express warranty. Additionally, the store, acting through its clerk, was a merchant because the store regularly dealt in beauty supply products, including the hair dye sold to the customer.

(Choice B) Disclaimers that grossly conflict with express warranties (e.g., "all warranties, express or implied, are disclaimed") are ignored. Accordingly, the clerk's attempt to disclaim her warranty with directly conflicting "as is" language was ineffective.

(Choice D) An implied warranty of fitness for a particular purpose can be disclaimed by conspicuous language in writing or by the use of language (e.g., "as is") that calls the buyer's attention to the exclusion of warranties and makes plain that there is no implied warranty. Therefore, the customer will likely prevail on her warranty claim because there was an express warranty that could not be disclaimed.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the UCC, a seller of goods creates an express warranty by making any promise or affirmation regarding the goods that becomes part of the basis of the bargain.

📚 References
  • U.C.C. § 2-313 (providing rules for creation of express warranties).
  • U.C.C. § 2-316 (discussing exclusion or modification of warranties).
questions.zh-question:
10月30日，一位顾客走进一家零售美容用品店，购买染发剂为万圣节染发。帮助该顾客的店员是前一天才雇用的，并未接受过关于不同类型染发剂的培训。顾客解释说她想要一种可洗的染发剂，因为她第二天有工作演示，需要看起来专业。店员向顾客展示了一种永久性染发剂，并向顾客保证该染发剂适合她的需求。店员随后告诉顾客，由于该染发剂正在促销，所以是“as is”（按现状）出售，并且她不负责任何不良反应。顾客购买并使用了该染发剂。11月1日早上，顾客无法将染发剂从头发上洗掉。结果，顾客因未能进行演示而失去了一个客户。
在针对该商店提起的违反保证之诉（breach-of-warranty action）中，顾客是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为该店员不是商人（merchant）。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为店员声明染发剂“as is”（按现状）出售，排除了任何保证（warranties）。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为店员的承诺构成了一项明示保证（express warranty）。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为特定目的适用性保证（warranty of fitness for a particular purpose）不能被免责（disclaimed）。

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：卖方对商品的口头保证，是否已经构成 明示保证（express warranty），从而让“as is”挡不住买家的索赔。

三秒认题路径：

买家说用途 → 店员保证 → 成交基础 → 货不符 → 明示保证成立

核心法律规则

抓住这条规则就够了

在 UCC 下，卖方只要对商品做出陈述、承诺、描述（affirmation / promise / description），而且这句话成了交易基础，就会形成 明示保证（express warranty）；考场意思：卖家不是在“夸一夸”，而是在给你一个能被追责的承诺。

相反，单纯的吹捧、意见或价值评价不算明示保证；但这题里店员不是说“我觉得不错”，而是直接说这种染发剂“适合你的需要”，所以已经把自己锁进了保证里。

“as is” 主要是想挡 默示保证（implied warranty），不是拿来轻松推翻已经成立的 明示保证（express warranty）。

核心判例： U.C.C. § 2-313 / § 2-316 - 本题的关键不是“有没有免责声明”，而是店员前面的承诺已经先把 express warranty 立起来了。

思维导图

先看：店员的话是在“夸”还是在“保证”？
题干触发：买家明确说要“可洗掉”的染发剂，店员却保证这款产品“适合她的需要”。
规则关卡：这类具体保证属于 affirmation / promise，只要成了交易基础，就会生成 express warranty。
卡死点：不是看卖家后来喊“as is”，而是先看前面的明示保证已经成立。
结果：货是永久染料、不能洗掉，说明承诺落空，买家可在 breach-of-warranty action 中赢。
结论：选 C

考点陷阱

你可能会想：店员已经说了“as is”，那所有保证都没了。

但考试真正问的是：这句话能不能打掉已经成立的 明示保证（express warranty），答案是不能。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干里店员明确说这款染发剂“适合她的需要”，这是 seller's assurance，已经把 明示保证（express warranty） 立起来了；后来产品洗不掉，正好证明保证被打破。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把明示保证误当成只限merchant才会有。

❌ 法律适用 | 中间上诉理由误判

✕ B: 以为一句as is就能直接抹掉前面的承诺。

❌ 事实误判 | 题干条件偷换

✕ D: 把本题硬套成fitness for a particular purpose。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓卖家有没有“保证”的话，再分清这是明示保证还是想拿免责声明去挡。

考场速记

记住一句：“先看卖家有没有承诺，再看免责声明能不能挡；有明示保证时，as is 通常救不了店家。”

口诀：“说到做到是明示；只会吹捧不是。”

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
An engineer signed a two-year contract to serve as the chief safety engineer for a coal mine at a salary of $7,000 per month. The position required the engineer to work underground each workday. After one week on the job, the engineer became very ill. He requested testing of the mine air system, which revealed the presence of a chemical agent to which the engineer had a rare allergic reaction. The engineer promptly quit. The coal mine then hired a qualified replacement for the remainder of the engineer's contract at a salary of $7,500 per month.
Assume that no statute or regulation applies.
If the coal mine sues the engineer for breach of contract, is the coal mine likely to recover damages?

choices.A: No, because an at-will employee has the right to terminate an employment contract.
choices.B: No, because the risk to the engineer's health excused his nonperformance of the contract.
choices.C: Yes, because the coal mine acted in good faith in mitigating the effect of the engineer's failure to finish the contract term.
choices.D: Yes, because the mine is reasonably safe for most people.

questions.explanation:
Ways to Discharge Contractual Obligations

Hover over the mnemonic letters or list items to see their connections

F Full performance of contractual obligations
I Impossibility, impracticability, or frustration of purpose
R Release (in writing only)
M Mutual rescission
S Substituted contract
C Contract or covenant not to sue
A Accord & satisfaction
N Novation
Mnemonic Device:
F I R M S C A N

A contract is rescinded (ie, canceled) due to the occurrence of an unexpected or extraordinary event if:

  • 1 that event makes it impossible or impracticable for one or both parties to perform their duties
  • 2 the contract was formed under a basic assumption that the event would not occur and
  • 3 neither party was at fault in causing the event to occur.

Rescission excuses both parties' nonperformance of the contract, which means that there can be no recovery of damages for breach.

Here, the engineer contracted to work in a mine each workday for two years. After one week, the engineer unexpectedly became very ill due to a rare allergy to a chemical in the mine—making it impracticable, if not impossible, for him to perform his duties. The parties must have assumed that the engineer did not have this rare allergy, and nothing indicates that either party caused the chemical's presence in the mine. Therefore, the engineer's health excused his nonperformance, and the coal mine is unlikely to recover damages.

Distinction & Choice Analysis

(Choice A)

The engineer was not an at-will employee since he agreed to work for a term of two years. But had he been one, he would have had the right to terminate his employment for any reason.

(Choice C)

After a breach of contract, the nonbreaching party must act in good faith in mitigating (ie, minimizing) his/her damages. But here, there was no breach since the engineer's nonperformance was excused.

(Choice D)

Although the mine is reasonably safe for most people, the doctrines of impossibility and impracticability apply even when one of the parties is particularly vulnerable to the unexpected event (as seen here).

Educational Objective

A contract is rescinded, and both parties' nonperformance is excused, when (1) an unexpected or extraordinary event makes it impossible or impracticable for one or both parties to perform, (2) the contract was formed under a basic assumption that the event would not occur, and (3) neither party was at fault in causing the event to occur.

References: Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 261 cmt. d (Am. Law Inst. 1981)

questions.zh-question:
一名工程师签订了一份为期两年的合同，在一家煤矿担任首席安全工程师，月薪为7000美元。该职位要求工程师每个工作日都在井下工作。上岗一周后，该工程师病得很重。他要求对矿井的空气系统进行检测，结果发现存在一种化学制剂，而该工程师对此有罕见的过敏反应。该工程师随即辞职。煤矿随后以每月7500美元的薪水，聘请了一名合格的替代者来完成该工程师合同的剩余期限。

假设没有任何法规或条例适用。

如果煤矿以违约为由起诉该工程师，煤矿是否可能获得损害赔偿？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为任意雇员有权终止雇佣合同。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为工程师的健康风险使其不履行合同的行为得到免责。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为煤矿在减轻因工程师未能完成合同期限所造成的影响方面，本着诚信原则行事。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为该煤矿对大多数人来说是合理安全的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Performance, Breach, and Discharge - Performance, Breach, and Discharge

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：合同履行中遇到impracticability（履行困难）时，是否可以把双方不履行都当成被免责，所以雇主不能拿“你没干完”去索赔。

三秒认题路径：

两年合同 → 突发重病 → 罕见过敏 → 履行变难 → 免责

核心法律规则

这题只要抓住这一条

履行不能/履行困难（impossibility / impracticability）的考场意思：不是“人想不想做”，而是“发生了合同外的突发事件后，按原计划继续履行已经不合理或做不到”。

如果事件是双方订约时没有预料到的、不是任何一方造成的，而且合同成立时默认这种事不会发生，非履行（nonperformance）就会被免责。这里工程师在井下工作后突然对矿内化学物质出现罕见过敏，正好落进这个规则，所以煤矿不能按违约拿损害赔偿。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 261 及其注释：意外事件让继续履行变得不切实际时，合同义务可以被解除。

思维导图

先问：这是不是“自己不想干了”？
不是。 题干给的是罕见过敏反应（rare allergy），属于突发健康事件，不是单纯跳槽或任性辞职。
再问：这种突发事件能不能把合同义务打断？
能，若满足： 意外事件（unexpected event） + 双方订约时默认不会发生 + 没有一方有过错。
卡死点：即使矿井对“多数人”安全，规则看的是这位工人是否被意外事件客观卡住，不看他是不是特别脆弱。
最后结论：
不能立刻追责。 工程师的非履行被免责，煤矿对剩余合同期的损失赔偿请求失败。
答案导向：选 B

考点陷阱

你可能会想：矿井对大多数人都算安全，那工程师自己体质特殊，就该自己承担后果。

但考试真正问的是：突发的罕见过敏是否让原本的工作义务变成了不切实际的履行，而不是看矿方有没有“主观上很坏”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 罕见过敏反应 让井下继续工作变得不切实际，属于免责事由，所以煤矿不能因剩余工期要求赔偿。

❌ 概念混淆 | 终身雇佣误判

✕ A: 这不是 at-will 雇佣，不能靠“想走就走”来解释。

❌ 法律适用 | 事后补救误判

✕ C: 这里先看有没有违约；既然已免责，就轮不到 mitigating 来救场。

❌ 事实误判 | 多数人安全偷换

✕ D: “对大多数人安全”不排除这位工程师被突发过敏卡死。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是否出现合同外突发事件，再判断是否把履行从“难做”推到“可免责”。

考场速记

记住一句：意外事件 + 非过错 + 基本假设被打破，就先想到 impracticability，不要急着往“违约赔钱”上套。

速记口诀：FIRM SCAN，本题用到的是 I = impossibility / impracticability / frustration；先抓免责，再看有没有损害赔偿。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A manufacturer of flat screen televisions and a big box retailer had a written contract in which the manufacturer agreed to sell and the retailer agreed to buy all of its requirements of a certain type of television for three years.
A dispute arose near the end of the third year, when the retailer returned 25 undefective televisions to the manufacturer for full credit along with a check payable to the manufacturer for the balance admittedly due on all other merchandise sold and delivered to the retailer. The check was conspicuously marked, "Payment in full for all goods sold to the retailer to date." The manufacturer's credit manager, reading this check notation and knowing that the retailer had also returned the 25 televisions for full credit, deposited the check without protest in the manufacturer's local bank account. The canceled check was returned to the retailer a week later.
Which of the following defenses would best serve the retailer in an action by the television manufacturer against the retailer for damages due to return of the 25 televisions?

choices.A: By depositing the check without protest and with knowledge of its wording, the television manufacturer discharged any remaining duty to pay on the part of the retailer.
choices.B: By depositing the check without protest and with knowledge of its wording, the television manufacturer entered into a novation discharging any remaining duty to pay on the part of the retailer.
choices.C: The parties' good-faith dispute over return of the televisions suspended the duty of the retailer, if any, to pay any balance due.
choices.D: The television manufacturer's deposit of the check and its return to the retailer after payment estopped the manufacturer thereafter to assert that the retailer owed any additional amount.

questions.explanation:
Offer to satisfy debt with check

  • Debtor tenders check clearly marked "payment in full"
    • Amount of debt undisputed
      • Check ≥ Debt
        ↓
        Debt satisfied
      • Check < Debt
        ↓
        Debt not satisfied
    • Amount of debt disputed
      • Creditor cashes check
        ↓
        Debt satisfied
      • Creditor rejects check
        ↓
        Debt not satisfied

When a debt is disputed in good faith, the debtor can attempt to settle the debt by giving the creditor a check conspicuously marked, "Payment in full." The creditor can then:

  • deposit the check – in which case the debtor's duty to pay is discharged or
  • reject the check – in which case the debtor's duty to pay is not discharged.

Here, the retailer disputed the amount owed to the television manufacturer since the retailer returned 25 undefective televisions for credit. The retailer included a check—conspicuously marked, "Payment in full"—in the amount of the balance due on all merchandise sold and delivered to the retailer other than the 25 undefective televisions. Therefore, the retailer's best defense is that, by depositing that check instead of rejecting it, the manufacturer discharged any remaining duty to pay on the part of the retailer.

(Choice B) A novation is a subsequent contract that substitutes a new party for one of the original parties. But here, the retailer attempted to settle a debt by tendering a check—not by substituting a new party.

(Choice C) When a debt is disputed in good faith, the debtor can attempt to settle the debt for less than the claimed amount. But the debtor is still required to pay the undisputed portion of the debt, if any.

(Choice D) The television manufacturer is estopped (ie, prohibited) from asserting a claim for any additional amount because the manufacturer deposited the check—not because the check was returned to the retailer after payment.

📌 Educational Objective

When the amount of a debt is disputed in good faith, the debtor can attempt to settle by giving the creditor a check conspicuously marked, "Payment in full." The debtor's duty to pay will be discharged only if the creditor deposits the check.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 281 cmt. d (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (explaining that a creditor who cashes a check marked "payment in full" may have formed an enforceable accord).
questions.zh-question:
一家平板电视制造商与一家大型零售商签订了一份书面合同，其中制造商同意出售，零售商同意在三年内购买其所需的全部某型号电视。

在第三年快结束时，双方发生了争议。零售商将25台无瑕疵的电视退还给制造商以获得全额退款，并附上一张支付给制造商的支票，用以支付除已退货商品外所有已售出并交付给零售商的公认到期余款。该支票上醒目地标注着：“全额付清迄今为止出售给零售商的所有商品款项。”制造商的信贷经理看到了支票上的标注，并且知道零售商已退回25台电视以获得全额退款，便将该支票存入了制造商的本地银行账户，且未提出异议。一周后，已兑现的支票被退还给零售商。

在电视制造商因零售商退回25台电视而对其提起的损害赔偿诉讼中，以下哪项抗辩最有利于零售商？

zh-choices.A: 电视制造商在知晓支票措辞的情况下，未经抗议地兑现了该支票，从而免除了零售商任何剩余的付款义务。
zh-choices.B: 电视制造商在知晓支票措辞的情况下，未经抗议地兑现了该支票，从而达成了一项债务更新（novation），免除了零售商任何剩余的付款义务。
zh-choices.C: 双方就退还电视一事存在的善意争议，中止了零售商支付任何到期余款的义务（若有）。
zh-choices.D: 电视制造商兑现支票并在付款后将其退还给零售商的行为，构成了禁止反言（estoppel），使制造商此后不得主张零售商拖欠任何额外款项。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Performance, Breach, and Discharge - Consideration

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：债务争议中的“支付全部”（payment in full）支票被债权人收下后，能不能把原债务一次性结清。

三秒认题路径：

有争议债务 → 付款全额支票 → 债权人存入 → 原债务消灭 → 选 A

核心法律规则

当债务金额存在善意争议（good-faith dispute）时，债务人可以交出一张明显写着“payment in full”的支票来做和解。考试意思很直接：债权人如果存入／兑现（cash/deposit）这张支票，通常就等于接受这个和解，剩余债务被清掉。

如果债权人拒收，债务人当然不能靠这张支票强行结案。这里的关键不是支票写得好不好看，而是债权人有没有把它收下。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 281 cmt. d — 债权人兑现标注“payment in full”的支票，可能形成可执行的和解协议（accord）。

思维导图

先看：这笔钱是不是有善意争议的债务？
是债务人可以开一张写明 payment in full 的支票。
再看债权人怎么做？
债权人存入／兑现 → 视为接受和解 → 剩余债务被消灭 → 选 A
债权人拒收 → 和解不成立 → 仍可继续追钱。
否若只是想把“债务争议”讲成别的制度，常见就会误走到 novation、estoppel 或“只暂停付款”的坑里。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然厂家知道支票写了“payment in full”，那是不是只要“收到支票”就当然还要再追余额。

但考试真正问的是：债权人有没有存入这张支票；一旦存入，命题人要你记住的是和解被接受，原来那笔争议债务就被结清了。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。本题不是在比谁更委屈，而是在看谁触发了“接受和解”这个法律后果。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干里支票明确写着“Payment in full”且厂家知道这一点后仍存入，这正是善意争议债务被接受和解的典型动作，故剩余债务被消灭。

❌ 概念混淆 | 新合同误套

✕ B: 把 novation 当成“收下支票”的效果了。

❌ 法律适用 | 停付误判

✕ C: 只盯着争议，不看厂家已收下 payment in full。

❌ 事实误判 | 事后寄回偷换

✕ D: 把“支票后来退回”硬说成关键，但真正触发后果的是先前的存入。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“争议债务 + 明示全额支票 + 债权人是否兑现”，再判断是否已经把和解收口。

考场速记

记住一句：争议债务 + payment in full + 债权人兑现 = 债务结清。看到这种题，先问“对方有没有存入支票”，别被返回电视、退货理由这些背景带跑。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A home goods distributor signed a written contract with a nursing home to sell the nursing home 100 identical bathroom sinks, 50 sinks to be delivered on March 1, and the remaining 50 sinks on April 1. The agreement did not specify the place of delivery, or the time or place of payment.
On March 1, the distributor tendered 49 sinks to the nursing home and explained, "One of the 50 sinks was damaged in transit from the manufacturer to us, but we will deliver a replacement within 5 days."
Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.A: The nursing home is entitled to accept any number of the 49 sinks and to reject the rest, but is not entitled to cancel the contract as to any rejected sinks or the lot due on April 1.
choices.B: The nursing home is entitled to accept any number of the 49 sinks, reject the rest, and cancel the contract, both as to any rejected sinks and the lot due on April 1.
choices.C: The nursing home must accept the 49 sinks and is not entitled to cancel the rest of the contract.
choices.D: The nursing home must accept the 49 sinks but is entitled to cancel the rest of the contract.

questions.explanation:
Buyer's rights under installment contract
(UCC § 2-612)
Each
installment
  • Buyer may reject nonconforming shipment that:
    • substantially impairs value of installment
    • cannot be cured
  • Buyer must accept:
    • conforming shipment
    • nonconforming shipment if seller promises to cure
Whole
contract
  • Buyer can cancel future installments if one or more nonconforming shipments substantially impair value of whole contract
  • Buyer cannot cancel future installments if he/she:
    • accepts nonconforming shipment without notice of cancellation
    • brings action only for past installments OR
    • demands performance of future installments
UCC = Uniform Commercial Code

Article 2 of the Uniform Commercial Code governs contracts for the sale of goods (e.g., sinks). Such contracts often call for the delivery of goods in separate lots (i.e., installment contracts). In that case, the buyer must accept each conforming shipment. But even if a shipment is nonconforming, the buyer must accept it if the seller gives adequate assurance that he/she will cure the nonconformity. And the buyer cannot cancel the rest of the contract unless the nonconforming shipment substantially impairs the value of the whole contract.

Here, the home goods distributor entered an installment contract for the delivery of 100 sinks in two separate lots. The first delivery was nonconforming since 1 of the 50 sinks was damaged. But the distributor offered to cure by delivering a replacement within five days. Therefore, the nursing home must accept the 49 sinks (Choices A & B). And since a short delay in the delivery of 1 sink does not substantially impair the value of the whole contract for 100 sinks, the nursing home is not entitled to cancel the rest of the contract (Choices B & D).

📌 Educational Objective

In an installment contract for the sale of goods, the buyer must accept a nonconforming shipment if the seller gives adequate assurance that he/she will cure the defect. And the buyer cannot cancel the rest of the contract unless the nonconforming shipment substantially impairs the value of the whole contract.

📚 References
  • U.C.C. § 2-612 (Am. Law Inst. & Unif. Law Comm'n 2020) (installment contracts).

3月1日，该经销商向疗养院交付了49个水槽，并解释说：“50个水槽中的一个在从制造商到我们这里的运输途中损坏了，但我们将在5天内交付替代品。”

下列哪个陈述是正确的？

zh-choices.A: 疗养院有权接受这49个水槽中的任何数量并拒收其余部分，但无权就任何被拒收的水槽或4月1日到期的那批货物取消合同。
zh-choices.B: 疗养院有权接受这49个水槽中的任何数量，拒收其余部分，并取消合同，包括任何被拒收的水槽和4月1日到期的那批货物。
zh-choices.C: 疗养院必须接受这49个水槽，并且无权取消合同的其余部分。
zh-choices.D: 疗养院必须接受这49个水槽，但有权取消合同的剩余部分。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Performance, Breach, and Discharge - Remedies Under the UCC

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：分批交付合同（installment contract）里，卖方这批货有瑕疵但承诺补救时，买方能不能拒收、能不能直接解除整份合同。

三秒认题路径：

分批交付 → 一批瑕疵 → 卖方可补救 → 先收货 → 不能解约

核心法律规则

只看这条就够做题

分批交付合同（installment contract）里，买方通常要接受每一批conforming shipment，也要接受卖方已经给出补救承诺（assurance to cure）的非符合货物，所以这题里 49 个完好洗手盆要先收下。

只有当这批非符合交付实质性影响（substantially impair）整份合同价值时，买方才可以把后续分批也一起取消；这里少 1 个、而且 5 天内补货，考试上不够把整份 100 个的合同打掉。

核心判例： UCC § 2-612 直接锁定：能补救的瑕疵交付，买方先收；只有整份合同价值被明显打垮，才轮到取消后续分批。

思维导图

先问：这是不是 分批交付合同（installment contract）？
是 题干写了 100 个同类洗手盆，分两批送货，直接落进 UCC § 2-612。
再问：这批货能不能直接拒收？
不能直接拒 卖方说 5 天内补一个 replacement，属于可补救；买方要先收 49 个。
最后问：能不能顺手把第二批也取消？
不能 只少 1 个、且很快补上，没到 substantially impair 整份合同价值的程度。
结论
答案 买方必须接受 49 个，不能取消剩余合同。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然有 1 个坏了，买方就能把这批和后面的都一起推掉。

但考试真正问的是：这 1 个瑕疵有没有大到把整份分批合同的价值都打坏；这里答案是否定的，所以不能取消后续分批。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的瑕疵有没有发生」。 这题里卖方已经给了补货时间，命题人就是想骗你把“小瑕疵”当成“整份合同报废”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干 5 天内补一个 replacement 说明卖方有补救承诺，所以 49 个先要收下；这点小瑕疵没把整份 100 个的合同价值打到可以解约。

❌ 概念混淆 | 只看局部拒收

✕ A: 你只盯着坏的那 1 个，忘了后续分批能不能一起取消。

❌ 法律适用 | 误把补救当解约

✕ B: 看到 cancel the contract 就冲动上车，但这里还没到整份合同受重挫。

❌ 事实误判 | 夸大瑕疵后果

✕ D: 把 1 个损坏说成足以让整份合同崩掉，题干没有这么强的事实。

这题建议用什么方法？

先认出 installment contract，再看卖方有没有 cure，最后只问这点瑕疵有没有打垮 whole contract。

考场速记

记住一句话：分批交付合同（installment contract）里，cure 先救单批，substantially impair 才能打到整份合同。

速记口诀：小瑕疵先补救，大伤害才解约。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
In the spring, a scholarship program held a competition to award $10,000 to the high school senior who wrote and submitted the best essay, as judged by the program's grading rubric. The competition announcement provided that any student could enter the contest by submitting an essay and a signed copy of the competition's "Terms and Conditions." Many students submitted essays, and the scholarship program selected a winner in accordance with their grading rubric the following fall. However, when the winning student tried to claim the award, the program refused to give it to him. The "Terms and Conditions" of the competition provided that the winner of the competition could receive the award only if he or she was enrolled in a public university in that state by the following fall. The winning student had not read the "Terms and Conditions" of the competition when he signed and submitted them with his essay and had already enrolled in an out-of-state private college by the fall.
If the winning student sues the scholarship program to recover the $10,000 award, will he succeed?

choices.A: No, because the student did not substantially perform under the terms of the competition.
choices.B: No, because the student was not enrolled in a public university in that state by the fall.
choices.C: Yes, because the student was unaware of the condition that he must be enrolled in a public university in that state by the fall.
choices.D: Yes, because the student wrote and submitted the best essay as judged by the program's grading rubric.

questions.explanation:
Contract conditions
Type of condition How created Performance required
Express
Set forth explicitly in contract Must be complied with fully; substantial performance does not suffice
Implied-
in-law
Supplied by court if reasonable under circumstances (i.e., constructive condition) Substantial performance suffices; full performance is not required
Implied-
in-fact
Nature of agreement suggests that parties intended condition but failed to expressly include it Substantial performance suffices; full performance is not required

Contracts may be subject to certain conditions (see image above), and a party's failure to perform such a condition relieves the other party of its contractual obligations. Express conditions are set forth explicitly in a contract and must be complied with fully unless excused. Mere substantial performance will not satisfy an express condition.

Here, the "Terms and Conditions" of the competition provided that the winner of the competition could receive the award only if he or she was enrolled in a public university in that state by the following fall. Although the winning student substantially performed by writing and submitting the best essay as judged by the program's grading rubric, he was not enrolled in a public university in the state by the fall (Choices A & D). And since the winning student failed to fully comply with this express condition, he will not succeed in a suit to recover the $10,000 award.

(Choice C) A party's failure to read an express condition to a contract does not excuse the party's failure to fully comply with the condition. Therefore, the fact that the winning student was unaware of the condition that he must be enrolled in a public university in the state by the fall is not a basis for him to recover the $10,000 award.

📌 Educational Objective

Express conditions are set forth explicitly in a contract and must be complied with fully unless excused. Mere substantial performance will not suffice to satisfy an express condition.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 252 (Am. L. Inst. 1981) (defining "express condition").
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 224 (Am. L. Inst. 1981) (explaining that a condition must occur, unless its nonoccurrence is excused, before performance under a contract becomes due).
questions.zh-question:
主题：Contracts — Performance, Breach, and Discharge

春季时，一个奖学金项目举办了一场比赛，向撰写并提交最佳 essay 的高中毕业班学生（high school senior）颁发 $10,000 奖金，该最佳 essay 由该项目的 grading rubric 评定。比赛公告规定，任何学生都可以通过提交一篇 essay 以及一份签字的比赛《Terms and Conditions》副本来参加。许多学生提交了 essay，奖学金项目于次秋按照其 grading rubric 选出了一名获奖者。然而，当该获奖学生试图领取奖金时，项目拒绝发放。该比赛《Terms and Conditions》规定，只有在次秋之前已在该州的一所 public university 注册入学，比赛获胜者才能获得奖金。该获奖学生在与 essay 一并签署并提交这些《Terms and Conditions》时，并未阅读其内容，而且到了秋季时，他已经入读了一所州外 private college。
如果该获奖学生起诉奖学金项目要求追回 $10,000 奖金，他会胜诉吗？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为该学生未依比赛条款 substantially perform。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为到秋季时，该学生并未在该州的一所 public university 注册入学。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为该学生并不知道自己必须在次秋之前就读于该州的一所 public university 这一条件。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为该学生按照该项目的 grading rubric 写并提交了最佳 essay。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Performance, Breach, and Discharge - Performance, Breach, and Discharge

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：明示条件（express condition）必须严格满足，不能拿“我已经大致做完了”来顶替。

三秒认题路径：

先看条件词 → 再看是否明示 → 不达成就别领钱 → 事后不读也不救 → 选不能赔

核心法律规则

只抓这一条就够

明示条件（express condition）是合同里写得很清楚的前提，考场意思：这个前提不发生，对方就不用付款或履行。

对明示条件（express condition），substantial performance 不够，必须 full compliance；所以只要条件没成，索赔就卡住。

“我没读条款”不改变结果，考场意思：签了就受约束，忘看、漏看、没看懂，都不是自动放行理由。

核心判例：Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 224 说明条件必须发生，除非其不发生被免除；本题就是条件没成，所以不给钱。

思维导图

先看条款是不是写了“只有满足某前提才给奖”
是这是 明示条件（express condition）
问：有没有 full compliance？
没有。只做了写作文，不代表满足“秋季前就读本州公立大学”
结果条件未成 → 对方无付款义务 → 不能拿 $10,000
别被带偏“没读条款”只说明他不知道，不等于条件消失
对应答案选 B

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他都写了最好的 essay，还拿到评分第一，应该算完成任务了。

但考试真正问的是：奖学金条款里那个入学条件（condition）有没有真正发生。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这里不是在算“表现得好不好”，而是在算“前提成没成”；前提没成，后面的领钱权就没开。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的关键事实是：条款明确要求他在秋季前就读本州公立大学；他没有做到，所以 明示条件（express condition）未成，不能拿奖。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把 substantially perform 当万能钥匙了；明示条件不是这么过关的。

❌ 事实误判 | 未读条款偷换

✕ C: 只因他没读条款就想放行，命题人骗你把“不知道”当“没约束”。

❌ 法律适用 | 评分结果误用

✕ D: 最高分只说明作文赢了，不代表 best essay 就自动满足领奖前提。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“只有在……才……”这种条件句，再直接问条件是否已发生；没发生就别往 substantial performance 上绕。

考场速记

记住一句：明示条件（express condition）要 full compliance，substantial performance 不够；看到“只有……才……”就先检查条件成没成，再决定能不能领结果。

question_analysis.skill_tested: applying express conditions to contract enforcement

reason.en: Represents the binding written rules governing the competition.
reason.zh: 代表规范比赛的具有约束力的书面条款。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
In a writing signed by both parties on December 1, a buyer agreed to buy from a seller a gasoline engine for $1,000, delivery to be made on the following February 1. Through a secretarial error, the writing called for delivery on March 1, but neither party noticed the error until February 1. Before signing the agreement, the parties orally agreed that the contract of sale would be effective only if the buyer should notify the seller in writing not later than January 2 that the buyer had arranged to resell the engine to a third person. Otherwise, they agreed orally, "There is no deal." On December 15, the buyer entered into a contract with a third party to resell the engine to the third party at a profit. The buyer did not give the seller notice of the resale agreement until January 25, and the seller received it by mail on January 26. In the meantime, the value of the engine had unexpectedly increased about 75% since December 1, and the seller renounced the agreement.
If the buyer sues the seller on February 2 for breach of contract, which of the following is the seller's best defense?

choices.A: In view of the unexpected 75% increase in value of the engine after December 1, the seller's performance is excused by the doctrine of commercial frustration.
choices.B: The agreement, if any, is unenforceable because a material term was not included in the writing.
choices.C: The buyer not giving written notice by January 2 of his resale agreement was a failure of a condition precedent to the existence of a contract.
choices.D: The secretarial error in the written delivery-term was a mutual mistake concerning a basic fact, and the agreement is voidable by either party.

questions.explanation:
Delay or discharge of performance
Contract formed
Condition occurs
Suit filed
Condition precedent
Performance delayed
➔
Performance due
➔
Plaintiff must prove to prevail
Condition subsequent
Performance due
➔
Performance discharged
➔
Defendant must prove to avoid liability

A party's performance under a contract can be made contingent upon the occurrence of a condition precedent. In that case, the party's performance will not become due until the condition occurs or its nonoccurrence is excused.

Here, the parties orally agreed that the contract would be effective only if the buyer gave the seller written notice by January 2 that the buyer had arranged to resell the gasoline engine (condition precedent). Because the buyer failed to notify the seller of his resale agreement until January 25 (nonoccurrence) and there is no indication that the condition's nonoccurrence was excused (eg, by waiver), the contract did not become effective. Therefore, the seller's best defense is that there was no breach due to failure of a condition precedent.

(Choice A) The doctrine of frustration of purpose applies only when the contract's purpose becomes worthless due to an unexpected event. But this doctrine is not available because a 75% increase in the gasoline engine's value is not an unexpected event that would render the sales contract worthless.

(Choice B) Contracts for the sale of goods (eg, gasoline engine) are governed by the UCC. The UCC specifically rejects the idea that a contract is unenforceable because it does not contain all material terms. Rather, the UCC limits enforcement of the contract to the quantity of goods in the writing (here, one gasoline engine).

(Choice D) When both parties are mistaken as to a contract's contents or legal effect (eg, due to a clerical error), reformation is available and neither party can avoid the contract.

📌 Educational Objective

When performance under a contract is contingent upon the occurrence of a condition precedent, performance is not due until the condition occurs or its nonoccurrence is excused.

UCC = Uniform Commercial Code

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 225 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (conditions and effect of nonoccurrence).
  • UCC § 2-201 (Am. Law Inst. & Unif. Law Comm'n 2020) (formal requirements for the sale of goods).

在一份由双方于12月1日签署的书面文件中，一名买方同意以1,000美元的价格从卖方处购买一台汽油发动机，并约定于次年2月1日交货。由于文书失误，书面文件要求于3月1日交货，但双方直到2月1日才注意到该错误。在签署协议之前，双方口头约定，仅当买方在1月2日之前书面通知卖方其已安排将该发动机转售给第三方时，该销售合同才生效。他们口头约定，否则“交易不成立”。12月15日，买方与第三方签订合同，以盈利价格将该发动机转售给第三方。买方直到1月25日才将转售协议通知卖方，卖方于1月26日通过邮件收到该通知。在此期间，自12月1日以来，该发动机的价值意外上涨了约75%，卖方因此宣布废除该协议。

如果买方于2月2日以违约为由起诉卖方，以下哪项是卖方最好的抗辩理由？

zh-choices.A: 鉴于12月1日后发动机价值意外上涨75%，根据商业目的落空原则，卖方的履约义务应被免除。
zh-choices.B: 该协议（如果存在）因书面文件中未包含重要条款而不可强制执行。
zh-choices.C: 买方未能在1月2日前就其转售协议发出书面通知，是合同成立的先决条件未能满足。
zh-choices.D: 书面交货条款中的文书失误是关于基本事实的共同错误，任何一方均可宣告该协议无效。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Performance, Breach, and Discharge - Timing of Conditions

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：口头约定把合同生效绑在一个先决条件（condition precedent）上，条件没按时发生，卖方就可以说根本没有可违约的合同。

三秒认题路径：

先决条件 → 期限未到 → 条件未成 → 合同未生效 → 卖方可抗辩

核心法律规则

这条规则怎么用

当双方把履行义务做成先决条件（condition precedent）时，履行（performance）要等条件发生后才“到期”。

考试里你要先问：这个条件有没有按约发生，或者有没有被豁免（excused）。如果没有，义务根本没启动，原告就很难证明被告违约。

本题里，写明“必须在 January 2 前书面通知”就是生效门槛，不是普通提醒；买方拖到 January 25 才通知，门槛没过，卖方最强抗辩就是未满足先决条件（failure of a condition precedent）。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 225 - 先决条件不发生时，履行义务不变为到期义务，除非该不发生被豁免。

思维导图

12/1 签字
书面合同已签，但口头把“生效”绑上通知门槛。
1/2 截止
应先通知已转售；没通知就是条件没成。
1/25 才通知
迟到的通知不能补回生效时点，除非有豁免。
2/2 起诉
decision-kill：条件未成 → 合同未生效 → 卖方不承担违约责任。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：价格突然涨了 75%，卖方是不是可以用 commercial frustration 或别的“公平理由”脱身。

但考试真正问的是：这题先看条件有没有成；条件没成，连“违约之后怎么免责”都还没轮到。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干的 January 2 书面通知 是合同生效门槛；买方到 January 25 才通知，条件没成，所以卖方可以说根本没有违约。

❌ 法律适用 | 免责规则误搬

✕ A: 把 commercial frustration 当成涨价借口了。

❌ 概念混淆 | UCC条款误判

✕ B: 看到少写细节就说合同无效，忽略了货物买卖下写明数量就够。

❌ 事实误判 | 误把笔误当核心

✕ D: 把 secretarial error 当主战场了，但这不是决定违约与否的点。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看条件是否成立，再谈违约；别被价格上涨和写作笔误带偏。

考场速记

记住一句：condition precedent 没发生，履行就还没到期，通常也谈不上违约。

看到“必须先通知、先批准、先发生某事才生效”，先把它翻成“门槛题”。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A woman owed her friend $5,000, plus interest at 6% until paid. Collection of the debt would become barred by the statute of limitations on July 31. On the preceding May 1, the woman and the friend both signed a writing in which the woman promised to pay the debt in full on the following December 31, plus interest at 6% until that date, and the friend promised not to sue to collect the debt in the meantime. The friend became concerned about the legal effect of the May 1 agreement, and on June 1 filed suit to collect the debt.
On January 2 of the following year, the friend's suit has not come to trial, and the woman has not paid the debt. The friend amends the complaint to add a second count to enforce the promise the woman made in the May 1 agreement.
Does the new count state a claim upon which relief can be granted?

choices.A: No, because such relief would undermine the policy of the statute of limitations against enforcement of stale claims.
choices.B: No, because the woman's May 1 promise was lawfully conditioned upon the friend's promise not to sue prior to December 31.
choices.C: Yes, because the woman's failure to pay the debt, plus interest, on December 31 makes the friend's breach of promise not to sue before that date no longer material.
choices.D: Yes, because the woman's May 1 promise is enforceable by reason of her moral obligation to pay the debt.

questions.explanation:
Common examples of constructive (ie, implied) conditions
Condition of performance
  • Each party's performance is conditioned on other party's performance
Condition of cooperation
  • Each party's performance is conditioned on other party's cooperation with that performance
Order of performance
  • Simultaneous performance possible – each party's performance is condition concurrent to other party's duty to perform (ie, performance due simultaneously)
  • One party's performance takes time – party's completion of longer performance is condition precedent to other party's duty to perform

A settlement agreement is a written and signed contract in which one party forgoes his/her right to sue on a claim in exchange for consideration. Unless stated otherwise, each party's duty to perform is impliedly conditioned upon the other party's performance. This means that a breach by one party excuses the nonbreaching party from performing, and the breaching party cannot enforce the agreement.

Here, on May 1, the woman and the friend signed a settlement agreement in which the woman agreed to repay her overdue debt by December 31, and the friend promised not to sue in the meantime. But the friend breached this agreement by filing suit on June 1. And since the woman's May 1 promise was lawfully conditioned upon the friend's promise not to sue before December 31, the woman was not required to repay the debt on December 31 **(Choice C)**. Therefore, the friend cannot enforce the May 1 agreement.

(Choice A) The underlying policy behind statutes of limitation is one of procedural fairness to the defendant—not one against the enforcement of stale claims.

(Choice D) A promise made out of a sense of moral obligation to compensate someone for a benefit previously received is generally unenforceable due to lack of consideration (ie, moral or past consideration). But here, the woman's promise to repay the debt by December 31 was made in exchange for the friend's promise not to sue—not because of the woman's moral obligation to pay the debt.

📌 Educational Objective

Unless stated otherwise, each party's duty to perform under a settlement agreement is conditioned upon the other party's performance. This means that a breach of the agreement excuses the nonbreaching party from performing, and the breaching party cannot enforce the agreement.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 74 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (settlement of claims).
questions.zh-question:
一名女子欠其朋友5,000美元，外加年利率6%的利息，直至付清为止。该债务的追偿将于7月31日因诉讼时效届满而无法执行。在此前的5月1日，该女子和朋友共同签署了一份书面文件，其中女子承诺在次年12月31日全额偿还债务，并支付截至该日的6%利息；朋友则承诺在此期间不起诉追讨该债务。朋友对5月1日协议的法律效力感到担忧，并于6月1日提起诉讼追讨该债务。

次年1月2日，朋友的诉讼尚未开庭审理，女子也未偿还债务。朋友修改了起诉状，增加了第二项诉讼请求，要求强制执行女子在5月1日协议中所作的承诺。

这项新的诉讼请求是否陈述了一项可以获得救济的主张？

zh-choices.A: 不可以，因为此种救济将损害诉讼时效制度旨在防止执行过期债权的政策。
zh-choices.B: 不可以，因为女子在5月1日的承诺，其法律上的生效条件是朋友承诺在12月31日之前不起诉。
zh-choices.C: 可以，因为女子未能在12月31日支付债务及利息，使得朋友在此日期前起诉的违约行为不再构成重大违约。
zh-choices.D: 可以，因为基于女子偿还债务的道德义务，其5月1日的承诺是可强制执行的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Performance, Breach, and Discharge - Timing of Conditions

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：和解协议里，除非另有约定，双方履行义务通常是互相附条件的；一方先违约，另一方就不用继续履行，违约方也不能拿这份协议来起诉对方。

三秒认题路径：

和解协议 → 先违约 → 条件未成就 → 对方免责 → 不能起诉

核心法律规则

和解协议（settlement agreement）是用“放弃起诉/暂缓起诉”换对价的合同。除非写明相反约定，双方的履行义务都默认为互为条件（implied condition），所以一方先违约，另一方可以不履行，违约方也不能强迫履行。

这里的关键是看谁先破坏了交换：朋友承诺“12月31日前不告”，这就是女人承诺“到12月31日再还钱”的前提条件。朋友在6月1日先起诉，等于先违约，所以女人到12月31日不必付款，朋友更不能再拿May 1协议逼她还钱。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 74 - 说明和解类协议里，除非另有约定，双方义务通常互为条件，先违约的一方不能主张对方履行。

思维导图

先看这是不是“交换承诺”的和解协议？
是女人还钱，朋友暂时不告，属于典型对价交换。
默认规则双方履行义务互为条件；breach（违约）会先把对方义务打掉。
本题卡点朋友在12月31日前就先起诉，直接违反“不起诉”承诺。
卡死结论：朋友先违约，女人到12月31日无需付款，朋友不能靠这份协议再告她。
答案选 B，不是 A / C / D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然原债务快到诉讼时效了，朋友再去告是不是只是“保全权利”。

但考试真正问的是：May 1 这份新协议能不能被执行，不是原债务值不值得追。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

别把“时效快到了”当成核心点；这题真正决定答案的，是朋友先违反了“不起诉”的交换承诺。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

朋友在 June 1 先起诉，先破坏了“不起诉到12月31日”的交换，所以女人到期不用付钱，这份新协议也不能被朋友拿来强制执行。

❌ 概念混淆 | 时效政策错位

✕ A: 把旧债时效问题当成新协议的无效理由，statute of limitations 不是这里的主规则。

❌ 法律适用 | 先违约忽略

✕ C: 只盯着女人没按时还钱，漏掉朋友先违背“不起诉”承诺这一刀。

❌ 事实误判 | 对价来源偷换

✕ D: 把 moral obligation 当成对价来源，但这份承诺是换来“不起诉”，不是道德还债。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看交换关系，再找谁先违约；和解协议题优先抓“互为条件”，不要被旧债背景带跑。

考场速记

记住一句：和解协议（settlement agreement）里，除非另有约定，双方义务通常互相附条件；谁先违约，谁就先失去强制对方履行的资格。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
Under a written agreement, a pastry supplier promised to sell its entire output of baked buns at a specified unit price to a retailer, for one year. The retailer promised not to sell any other supplier's baked buns.
Shortly after making the contract, and before the supplier had tendered any buns, the retailer decided that the contract had become undesirable because of a sudden, sharp decline in its customers' demand for baked buns. It renounced the agreement, and the supplier sues for breach of contract.
Which of the following will the court probably decide?

choices.A: The retailer wins, because mutuality of obligation was lacking in that the retailer made no express promise to buy any of the supplier's baked buns.
choices.B: The retailer wins, because the agreement was void for indefiniteness of quantity and total price for the year involved.
choices.C: The supplier wins, because the retailer's promise to sell the supplier's baked buns exclusively, if it sold any such buns at all, implied a promise to use its best efforts to sell the supplier's one-year output of baked buns.
choices.D: The supplier wins, because under the applicable law both parties to a sale-of-goods contract impliedly assume the risk of price and demand fluctuations.

questions.explanation:
Output v. Requirements contracts
(UCC § 2-306)
Output Contract for sale of as many goods as seller produces during specified period
Requirements Contract for sale of as many goods as buyer requires during specified period
UCC = Uniform Commercial Code.

Article 2 of the Uniform Commercial Code (UCC) governs contracts for the sale of goods (eg, baked buns). Under the UCC, a contract for exclusive dealing in the type of goods concerned (eg, output or requirements contract) carries with it an implied obligation by the seller to use its best efforts to supply the goods and by the buyer to promote their sale.

Here, the pastry supplier promised to sell its entire output of baked buns to the retailer for one year. The retailer made no express promise to buy any of the supplier's baked buns. But since the retailer promised to sell the supplier's baked buns exclusively, if it sold any such buns at all, the retailer impliedly promised that it would use its best efforts to sell the supplier's one-year output of baked buns (Choice A). Therefore, the supplier probably wins.

(Choice B) Contracts for the sale of goods must contain definite terms that (1) reasonably identify the goods to be sold and (2) specify a quantity of goods to be sold that is certain or capable of being made certain by reference to objective facts. The quantity term is sufficiently definite in output contracts (as seen here) since the seller's actual output can be determined objectively.

(Choice D) Although both parties to a sale-of-goods contract impliedly assume the risk of price and demand fluctuations, this is not a basis for the supplier's success. Instead, the supplier will win because the retailer is required to use its best efforts to sell the supplier's baked buns.

📌 Educational Objective

Contracts for exclusive dealing in the type of goods concerned carry with them an implied obligation by the seller to use its best efforts to supply the goods and by the buyer to promote their sale.

📚 References
  • UCC § 2-306 (output, requirements, and exclusive dealings).
questions.zh-question:
根据一份书面协议，一家糕点供应商承诺在一年内以指定的单价将其生产的全部烤面包出售给一家零售商。零售商承诺不销售任何其他供应商的烤面包。

签订合同后不久，在该供应商交付任何面包之前，零售商因其顾客对烤面包的需求突然急剧下降，认为该合同对其不利。零售商宣布废除该协议，供应商遂以违约为由提起诉讼。

法院可能会做出以下哪项判决？

zh-choices.A: 零售商胜诉，因为缺乏对等义务，零售商并未明确承诺购买供应商的任何烤面包。
zh-choices.B: 零售商胜诉，因为协议因数量和年度总价不确定而无效。
zh-choices.C: 供应商胜诉，因为零售商承诺独家销售供应商的烤面包（如果它销售任何此类面包的话），这默示了其承诺将尽最大努力销售供应商一整年产量的烤面包。
zh-choices.D: 供应商胜诉，因为根据适用法律，货物买卖合同的双方都默示地承担了价格和需求波动的风险。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Performance, Breach, and Discharge - Performance, Breach, and Discharge

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：输出合同（output contract）和独家交易（exclusive dealing）里，卖方只要约定独家卖货，买方就会被默认为要“尽最大努力”帮它卖货，所以不能拿“我没明说要买”来直接脱身。

三秒认题路径：

卖整季产量 → 独家销售 → 默认 best efforts → 不是无对价 → 选供应商赢

核心法律规则

UCC 第2-306条（UCC § 2-306）管货物买卖里的输出合同（output contract）和需求合同（requirements contract）。考试意思：数量不一定要写死，只要能按卖方实际产量或买方实际需求客观确定，就不是“太不确定”。

更关键的是，独家交易（exclusive dealing）合同会自动带进善意与最佳努力（best efforts）义务；卖方要尽力供货，买方要尽力促销。考试上所以不能因为买方没明说“我一定买多少”就说合同没约束力。

核心判例： UCC § 2-306 锁定本题：独家经销不是“随便不卖”，而是默认要尽最大努力推销对方产品。

思维导图

先看是不是 货物买卖，而且是一方卖“整年产量”给另一方？
是：进入 输出合同（output contract） / 独家交易（exclusive dealing）。
再看：买方是否只卖这一家的独家烤面包？
是：法律自动补进 best efforts。
卡死点：不是看“有没有明说必须买”，而是看“独家关系里有没有默认促销义务”。
结果：买方不能因需求下跌就单方撕约，供应商赢。
不是：如果只是想抓“数量不明”，先别急，输出量可由客观产量确定，不会因这一点无效。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：买方根本没承诺买多少，需求又暴跌了，所以它可以直接说合同没约束力。

但考试真正问的是：独家经销里会不会自动补进best efforts 义务；答案是会，所以不能拿“我没写明买入数量”来逃。

司法考试看的是「合同法上有没有默认救济义务」，而不是「市场需求是不是突然变差」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干写的是整年output of baked buns加上独家销售，这会触发best efforts默认义务，所以供应商可以赢。

❌ 概念混淆 | 互惠误判

✕ A: 把mutuality当成必须明说买多少，忽略了独家关系自带义务。

❌ 事实误判 | 数量不定误判

✕ B: 题干的数量可按卖方实际产量客观确定，不是“写不清就无效”。

❌ 法律适用 | 风险承担错位

✕ D: 需求波动不是卖方输的原因，买方没尽力促销才是关键。

这题建议用什么方法？

先识别 output / exclusive dealing，再直接套 UCC § 2-306 的默认 best efforts 规则。

考场速记

记住一句：输出合同看客观产量，独家交易看默认best efforts；别被“没明说买多少”骗到。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A buyer agreed to purchase a seller's house for $250,000 "on condition that the buyer obtain mortgage financing within 30 days." Thirty days later, the buyer told the seller that he would not purchase the house because he had not obtained mortgage financing. The seller asked the buyer where he had tried to obtain mortgage financing, and the buyer responded, "I was busy and didn't have time to seek mortgage financing."
If the seller sues the buyer for breach of contract, is the court likely to find the buyer in breach?

choices.A: No, because the buyer's performance was subject to a condition that did not occur.
choices.B: No, because the promise was illusory since the buyer was not obligated to do anything.
choices.C: Yes, because a promise was implied that the buyer had to make reasonable efforts to obtain mortgage financing.
choices.D: Yes, because a reasonable interpretation of the agreement is that the buyer had an obligation to purchase the house for $250,000 in 30 days.

questions.explanation:
Delay or discharge of performance
Contract formed
Condition occurs
Suit filed
Condition precedent
Performance delayed
➔
Performance due
➔
Plaintiff must prove to prevail
Condition subsequent
Performance due
➔
Performance discharged
➔
Defendant must prove to avoid liability

A binding contract is formed when one party makes an offer and the other party accepts. Performance is generally due once the contract is formed but performance can be contingent upon the occurrence of a condition. There are two types of conditions:

  • condition precedent* – delays performance until a specified event occurs
  • condition subsequent – excuses performance once a specified event occurs

If a party whose duty to perform is subject to a condition precedent wrongfully prevents the condition from occurring—eg, by breaching the implied duty of good faith and fair dealing—then the condition will be excused. In other words, the condition no longer needs to occur for that party's performance to become due.

Here, the agreement to purchase the house was conditioned on the buyer's ability to obtain financing within 30 days. The implied duty of good faith and fair dealing required the buyer to make reasonable efforts to secure financing. But since the buyer breached that duty by making no effort to obtain financing, the condition precedent was excused and his performance became due. Therefore, the court is likely to find the buyer is in breach (Choice A).

*A condition concurrent arises when each party's obligation to perform is a condition precedent to the other party's obligation to perform (ie, when performance is due simultaneously).

(Choice B) A promise is illusory, and therefore unenforceable, if the promisor can choose whether to honor it—eg, had the buyer promised to purchase the house "if I want to." Here, however, the buyer's promise was not illusory because it implicitly obligated him to make efforts to obtain financing within 30 days.

(Choice D) The duty of good faith and fair dealing did not require the buyer to purchase the house but rather to make a reasonable effort to obtain financing within 30 days.

📌 Educational Objective

If a party whose duty to perform is subject to a condition precedent wrongfully prevents that condition from occurring—eg, by violating the implied duty of good faith and fair dealing—the condition will be excused and that party must perform.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 225 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (effect of a nonoccurrence of a condition).
questions.zh-question:
一位买方同意以250,000美元的价格购买卖方的房屋，“条件是买方在30天内获得抵押贷款融资。”三十天后，买方告知卖方他将不购买该房屋，因为他没有获得抵押贷款融资。卖方询问买方曾在何处尝试获得抵押贷款融资，买方回答说：“我太忙了，没有时间去寻求抵押贷款融资。”

如果卖方以违约为由起诉买方，法院是否可能认定买方违约？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为买方的履行取决于一个未发生的条件。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为该承诺是虚幻的，因为买方没有义务做任何事情。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为存在一项默示承诺，即买方必须做出合理努力以获得抵押贷款融资。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为对协议的合理解释是，买方有义务在30天内以250,000美元购买该房屋。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Performance, Breach, and Discharge - Timing of Conditions

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：条件先决（condition precedent）被一方自己故意不做成时，法院会不会把这个条件豁免（excused），然后直接认定他该履行。

三秒认题路径：

条件先决 → 不去办贷款 → 违反诚信 → 条件被豁免 → 卖方可赢

核心法律规则

这题只用这一条规则

条件先决（condition precedent）的意思是：先等某个事件发生，履行义务才到期，所以它本来会延后履行（delay performance）。

但如果负有履行义务的一方故意阻止条件发生（wrongfully prevent the condition），就会违反诚实信用与公平交易义务（implied duty of good faith and fair dealing），法院会把这个条件当作已经被豁免（excused）。

这时考试结论不是“条件没成所以我不用做”，而是“你自己把条件搞没了，所以履行义务反而到期了”。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 225 - 条件不发生的一般后果：若条件被错误阻止，法院可把条件视为已被豁免。

思维导图

合同成立
买卖合同先成立，正常情况下买方有付款/购买义务。
30天内
获得按揭融资（mortgage financing）是条件先决（condition precedent）。
买方什么都没做
他说“我太忙，没去找贷款”，这就是自己把条件卡死。
法律后果
违反诚信义务 → 条件被豁免 → 付款义务到期。
诉讼结论
卖方能证明买方该履行却没履行，所以买方违约。
卡死点：不是看“条件没发生”，而是看“谁害条件没发生”。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：题目写的是“没拿到融资”，那就直接说条件没成（condition did not occur），所以买方不用买。

但考试真正问的是：买方有没有先违反善意努力（reasonable efforts），自己把这个条件弄没了。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这题的陷阱是把“没发生条件”当成免责理由；真正区分点是：条件是被自然没发生，还是被你自己不作为搞没。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干明确写出买方“没时间去找贷款”，这是对30天内取得融资这一条件先决（condition precedent）的消极阻止；因此法院会推定他有合理努力（reasonable efforts）义务，条件被豁免后反而构成违约。

❌ 事实误判 | 条件未分清

✕ A: 把“条件没成”当成免责，但忽略了他自己没去办贷款。condition precedent

❌ 概念混淆 | 单方随意误判

✕ B: 误把“先要努力申请融资”说成完全不用做任何事。illusory

❌ 法律适用 | 直接购买偷换

✕ D: 把合同读成“无条件30天内必须买房”，偷换了reasonable interpretation。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓条件类型，再问是谁阻止了条件发生，最后看诚信义务有没有把条件直接“救活”。

考场速记

记住一句：条件先决（condition precedent）不是天然免死金牌；自己把条件弄没了，条件就可能被豁免，履行义务照样到期。

考场口诀：“先等条件，后看谁害条件没成。”

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A life coach entered into a contract with an introverted woman to provide a weeklong course that served as an introduction to the life coach's yearlong program. Under the terms of the contract, the life coach would work with the woman full-time for a week to start teaching her to interact with people with more confidence. The woman would then participate in a speed-dating event as her "graduation" from the course. The contract also provided that unless the woman received an offer for a second date at the speed-dating event, she had no obligation to pay for the introductory course. If she received an offer for a second date at the speed-dating event, she would be required to pay the life coach $1,000 within three days of the event.
After working with the life coach pursuant to the terms of the contract, the woman attended the speed-dating event. Four days after the event, when the woman still had not paid the life coach, the life coach brought a breach-of-contract action against the woman to recover $1,000 under the contract.
Which of the following best states the burden of proof that will apply in this case?

choices.A: Because the contract involved a condition precedent, the life coach must prove that the woman received an offer of a second date at the speed-dating event to recover.
choices.B: Because the contract involved a condition precedent, the woman must prove that she did not receive an offer of a second date at the speed-dating event to avoid liability.
choices.C: Because the contract involved a condition subsequent, the life coach must prove that the woman received an offer of a second date at the speed-dating event to recover.
choices.D: Because the contract involved a condition subsequent, the woman must prove that she did not receive an offer of a second date at the speed-dating event to avoid liability.
